subject: Customer dashboard access & exception request for throughput/latency metrics

Subject: Procurement questionnaire — metrics, dashboards, and exception process

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Procurement at ACME asked for a short writeup to close our security and SRE checklist. They want to confirm: how Redwood measures uptime and p99/p95 latency for customer traffic, what monitoring we provide to customers (dashboard and raw metrics access), alerting channels, and the formal route if we need an SLO exception (e.g., planned maintenance, bursty events).

Concretely, can you provide:
- A one-page description of the metric definitions (availability, p95/p99 latency) and sampling window used for contracts
- Which dashboards we can share (real-time, 1m/5m/1h aggregations) and any redaction rules
- Whether ACME can receive Prometheus-compatible metrics or a read-only Grafana link, and how to request it
- The escalation path and doc we use to approve temporary SLA exceptions (owner, lead times, evidence required)

Procurement prefers doc + a limited-demo link they can hand to SRE. They also attached their exception request template (see attached). Can you loop in anyone technical if needed?

Appreciate it — Elaine

--
Elaine Wong
Director, Platform Procurement | ACME Corp

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T18:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — metrics, dashboards, and exception process

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list. I put together a short overview and attached a PDF (redwood-slo-metrics-overview.pdf) that covers definitions, measurement windows, and the dashboard options we can provision to customers. High-level answers below and a proposed next step.

Quick answers:
- Measurement: Availability = successful-response-rate measured at the API ingress per minute; we calculate rolling 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day windows. Latency: p50/p95/p99 computed on server-side end-to-end request time (token-generation cut included) sampled per request. Contract SLOs reference the 30-day rolling window unless otherwise specified.
- Dashboards: We can provide a read-only Grafana instance that includes 1m, 5m, and 1h aggregations plus raw request histograms. We also provide a streaming timeline and token-cost breakdown on the console. Redactions: payloads and prompt texts are not exposed by default; request metadata (status codes, regions, model variant, latency) is visible.
- Metrics access: Two options — (1) read-only Grafana link with RBAC and IP allowlist, or (2) Prometheus push gateway/metrics export for dedicated/private deployments. For hosted customers we typically do option (1); for Dedicated we can set up Prometheus scraping.
- Exception process: We have a documented Exception Request form (owner: ProdOps; SLA exceptions require 48-72 hour lead time unless emergency), evidence required: outage timeline, mitigation actions, and rollback plan. Post-approval we issue a temporary SLA amendment and update the billing credits if applicable.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Karthik (technical) to confirm the Grafana scope and Rachel on the CS side for the access workflow. If you want the read-only dashboard preview today, I can create a 72-hour demo link scoped to ACME SREs.

-Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@acmecorp.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T19:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — metrics, dashboards, and exception process

Hi Elaine — quick technical clarifications from our side:

1) Latency measurement details: We compute p95/p99 on server-side request completion time (time from HTTP ingress to final token flush). For multi-part streaming sessions we compute both token-emit latency and overall request completion. Sampling: all requests are recorded; histograms are aggregated with HDR histograms to preserve tail accuracy without excessive cardinality.

2) Alerting: Alerts can be pushed to PagerDuty, Slack, or email. By default we create service-level alerts for sustained error-rate > 1% over 5 minutes and latency degradation > 30% relative to baseline for 10 minutes. We can tune thresholds per-customer in the onboarding playbook.

3) Dashboard access: The read-only Grafana link will not expose prompt text or uploaded data. For customers that require raw telemetry we offer an export CSV or a Prometheus endpoint in Dedicated mode.

I attached a short checklist (not the PDF) for our SRE onboarding; happy to walk ACME's SRE through the Grafana panels tomorrow.

-karthik

--

Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
